Okali est une filiale de La Fabrique by CA, startup studio Corporate du Groupe Credit Agricole, spécialisé en fintech.

Pionnier de la Bank-As-A-Service, Okali, accompagne les entreprises et les fintechs dans la conception, le développement et le pilotage de solutions de paiement innovantes. Nous avons notamment contribué à la naissance et au développement d’entreprises à succès telles que Lydia, Spendesk, Blank ou encore Limonetik.

Okali est un acteur bancaire dont le métier est avant tout opérationnel : exécuter des paiements, entrer en relation avec les clients, gérer le cycle de vie des comptes et assurer la conformité de chaque opération. Notre plateforme repose sur deux briques complémentaires. Le moteur de traitement bancaire traite les fichiers ISO 20022 (PACS, CAMT, PAIN), l'ensemble des messages SEPA via son module dédié, les échanges EBICS et l'intégration avec les systèmes cœur de banque. La plateforme de connaissance client porte notre Back Office, l'outil quotidien des équipes opérations et conformité pour décider sur les personnes, les comptes, les virements, les cartes, le screening, les saisies et les déblocages de fonds.

En tant que Développeur Full Stack Senior, vous intervenez sur toute la chaîne, du modèle de données jusqu'à l'interface utilisateur. Les données manipulées sont sensibles et une erreur a des conséquences réelles : un compte suspendu bloque toutes ses opérations, un déblocage libère des fonds. C'est pourquoi notre front, en React 19, doit être maîtrisé en profondeur : les fiches de décision agrègent plusieurs sources, les listes sont volumineuses et les parcours multi-étapes exigent une validation rigoureuse. Vous êtes aussi un point d'appui pour l'équipe : vous prenez des décisions techniques, vous les argumentez et vous aidez chacun à progresser.

Vos missions

  • Concevoir et faire évoluer les services back-end en TypeScript (NestJS, Fastify) et les API GraphQL, en arbitrant entre performance, sécurité et maintenabilité.
  • Faire évoluer le Back Office React : nouvelles fonctionnalités, performances et ergonomie, en lien étroit avec les équipes opérations et conformité.
  • Modéliser et faire évoluer les données avec Prisma et PostgreSQL, en pensant migrations, intégrité et volumétrie.
  • Intervenir sur les traitements de fichiers bancaires (ISO 20022, EBICS) et sur les flux asynchrones (SQS, workers, tâches planifiées).
  • Participer à la chaîne de livraison : tests, revues de code, déploiements conteneurisés sur AWS.
  • Garantir la qualité et la sécurité de vos livrables, en tenant compte des exigences réglementaires du secteur bancaire.
  • Transmettre : accompagner des profils moins expérimentés, partager les bonnes pratiques et documenter les choix d'architecture.

Notre stack technique

Côté traitement bancaire, nous travaillons avec Node.js 26, TypeScript, NestJS 11 sur Fastify, Prisma 7 et PostgreSQL, Redis, et les services AWS (S3, SQS, etc .), avec Jest pour les tests. Côté connaissance client, la stack repose sur Bun, GraphQL (graphql-yoga et Pothos), React et une bibliothèque de composants interne, avec WebAuthn pour l'authentification sans mot de passe. L'ensemble est conteneurisé avec Docker, déployé sur AWS (ECS Fargate) et décrit en Terraform et Terragrunt. L'outillage s'appuie sur Yarn, ESLint, Prettier et Husky.

Vous n'êtes pas attendu sur l'ensemble de cette stack dès le premier jour. Nous recherchons avant tout une personne capable d'apprendre vite, de remettre en question nos choix quand c'est pertinent et d'en proposer de meilleurs.

Votre profil

Nous valorisons au même niveau vos compétences techniques et vos qualités humaines. Un profil senior, pour nous, sait faire et sait faire ensemble.

Sur le plan technique, vous maîtrisez TypeScript et Node.js en production, avec une expérience du back-end sous NestJS (ou un framework équivalent), des API REST et GraphQL, et une modélisation PostgreSQL où les migrations de schéma restent sous contrôle. Vous êtes à l'aise en React : gestion d'état, performances sur les grandes listes, formulaires et accessibilité. Vous savez traiter des flux asynchrones (files de messages de type SQS, workers, tâches planifiées), écrire des tests unitaires. La sécurité applicative, la connaissance de la conformité (RGPD, connaissance client, secteur bancaire) et des formats ISO 20022, EBICS ou virements SEPA sont des atouts appréciés. Une expérience de Jira est attendue : vous savez rédiger des tickets explicites, avec un objectif clair, un périmètre défini, des critères d'acceptation et un découpage en sous-tâches (développement, tests, vérification). Dans un métier aussi régulé que la banque, cette traçabilité n'est pas une formalité : elle permet de justifier chaque évolution auprès des équipes conformité et des auditeurs.

Vous utilisez l'IA générative au quotidien, avec discernement : pour gagner du temps sur le code, les tests et la documentation, en relisant et en testant systématiquement ce qu'elle produit, et en ne lui confiant jamais de données clients. Savoir expliquer comment et pourquoi vous l'employez compte autant, pour nous, que le résultat obtenu.

Sur le plan humain, vous êtes autonome : vous cadrez un sujet flou, le découpez et le livrez sans attendre d'être guidé à chaque étape. Vous savez expliquer un choix technique à un interlocuteur non technique et vous travaillez en confiance avec les équipes produit, opérations et conformité. Vous accueillez les retours avec recul et savez en tirer le meilleur parti. Le code, les tests et la documentation sont pour vous des livrables à part entière, et vous aimez faire monter les autres en compétence. Enfin, vous assumez vos décisions, y compris lorsqu'il faut les corriger.

Okali recrute sur les compétences et le potentiel. Nous encourageons toutes les candidatures, y compris celles dont le parcours ne suit pas le schéma classique. Si certains points de cette fiche vous semblent hors de portée, postulez quand même : nous évaluons ce que vous savez faire et ce que vous souhaitez apprendre.

12-month fixed-term contract | Global Revenue Systems and AI Team |


About the Role

Our reps spend most of their day in Salesforce, and how it feels to use directly affects how much they sell. We're hiring a Salesforce Developer with a UI/UX focus to redesign the rep experience across our Sales and Revenue teams. You'll join the global Salesforce team for 12 months to make the CRM faster, clearer and more intuitive.

This is a hands-on build role. You'll design the experience and code it in Lightning Web Components, working with Sales, RevOps, Marketing and Data, and directly with the reps who use the result.


What You Will Do


Redesign the rep experience

  • Audit the current Lightning experience (record pages, console apps, list views, home pages) and find where reps lose time to clicks, clutter and missing context.

  • Turn what you find into a prioritised roadmap of UI improvements tied to rep productivity and adoption.

  • Design and prototype improved layouts, workflows and components, and validate them with reps before building.

Build with LWC

  • Develop custom Lightning Web Components (and supporting Apex where needed) that replace clunky standard layouts with focused, usable interfaces.

  • Configure and extend Lightning App Builder pages, Dynamic Forms, Dynamic Actions and console apps to deliver a consistent experience across teams and regions.

  • Build reusable components and follow SLDS conventions so the UI stays consistent and maintainable after your contract ends.

Make it stick

  • Run feedback sessions, usability tests and pilots with reps and managers, and iterate on the results.

  • Track adoption, page performance and user satisfaction to show what each release changed.

  • Create release notes, short walkthroughs and handover documentation so changes land well and the team can maintain what you build.

Work as part of the global team

  • Work within the global team's standards for source control, code review, sandboxes and release management.

  • Partner with admins, architects and data teams so UI changes fit the wider data model, security model and automation.

  • Pass on what you learn about Lightning UX patterns and LWC best practices to the wider team.


What You Will Need


Must have

  • Strong, demonstrable experience building Lightning Web Components in production.

  • Solid Apex, SOQL and Salesforce data model knowledge to support your components.

  • Deep knowledge of Lightning Experience customisation: App Builder, Dynamic Forms, page layouts, console apps and Flows.

  • Experience with Salesforce DX, Git and a CI/CD or deployment process.

  • A UX mindset: you start from user problems, can explain design decisions, and can take feedback from non-technical users.

  • Clear communication and the ability to work independently across time zones in a global team.

Nice to have

  • Portfolio or examples of Salesforce UI work you've shipped (screenshots or demos are ideal).

  • Experience with SLDS, Figma or similar prototyping tools, and accessibility (WCAG) principles.

  • Experience in Sales Cloud, especially rep-facing workflows such as opportunity management, account planning and pipeline views.

  • Jest testing for LWC, and Salesforce certifications (Platform Developer I/II, JavaScript Developer I, Platform App Builder).

  • Experience with performance profiling and optimisation in Lightning pages.


What Success Looks Like (12 Months)

  • Month 3: UX audit complete and a prioritised roadmap agreed with Sales leadership.

  • Month 6: First wave of redesigned pages and components live for a pilot group, with adoption and feedback baselined.

  • Month 12: Redesigned experience rolled out to target teams, a maintained component library in place, and full documentation handed to the global team.

What we offer

  • Join our unforgettable Perk events, including our spectacular annual summer party

  • Always feel supported with Spring Health, our market-leading wellbeing partner, providing fast, comprehensive access to 12x therapy and 12x coaching sessions for you and your loved ones

  • Focus on your family with 12-16 weeks’ paid parental leave

  • Broaden your horizons with up to 20 "Work from Anywhere" days per year

  • Stay savvy with access to a wide variety of discounts and rewards

  • Follow your passions and take a four-week, fully paid sabbatical once you reach 5 years

AI at Perk
AI is embedded in how we work across every function. The tools you'll use day-to-day are AI-enabled so you can move faster and spend more time on the work that matters. In practice, that means using AI to research and prioritise accounts, draft and refine outreach, handle customer interactions more effectively, synthesise information, and cut through shadow work - the invisible tasks that pull people away from the work only they can do - so you can focus on relationships and outcomes.

Every medical practice runs on software that holds its calendar and its patients. There are dozens of different ones. Most were built twenty years ago and some have no API at all. TypeScript everywhere (Node, monorepo), PostgreSQL, REST and SOAP APIs from software vendors.

  • For this role we are looking a the senior who frames the work first, sets guardrails and reviews carefully.

  • We talk every day with the ops team that deploys clinics and the support team that hears when something breaks.

  • 700+ industrial sites equipped across 43+ countries.
  • Reference customers such as Safran, Airbus, Renault, Scania, LVMH, Andros, Bel, Merck and Lonza.

  • A team of :140 people, and an AI roadmap that is already in customers' hands rather than on a slide.
  • The role

Context: You join Fabriq's AI team, currently a three-person unit led by Jean (Product Lead) alongside two Senior Engineers: Halim & Rafik. This team operates as a prototyping squad at the front edge of the company: it tests new ideas, measures market appetite and decides whether Fabriq goes there. Products are in alpha, cycles are short, the roadmap is directional. The team also works weekly with Octave, co-founder, which gives you direct exposure to the strategic decisions.

Objective: Become the third engineer on AI alongside Halim and Rafik, reach full autonomy on the stack and the customer context within 6 months, and take Fabriq's AI products from alpha to something industrial teams rely on every day.

Challenges:

  • Taking AI prototypes to production quality. Conversational and voice-driven agents, plugged into real industrial data and used by real teams on the floor. You take them from alpha to something people rely on daily: answer quality, reliability, and the cost per interaction that decides whether a use case scales or gets dropped.
  • Prototyping to convince. Part of the roadmap is co-built with partner customers, which means it is sold before it is built. Specs move as customers shape them, timelines are tight, and you build fast to prove a use case is worth pursuing. Testing a lot and abandoning a lot is part of the deal.
  • Agentic engineering from scratch. No Mastra, no LangGraph, no off-the-shelf framework. Everything is hand-built in TypeScript and Deno on top of frontier models called through AWS Bedrock. When the team needs something like agent memory compaction, you design it yourself. This is custom, sparsely documented territory, and that is precisely the technical interest of the role.
  • Setting the technical direction with Halim and Rafik. You are the third engineer, not an extra pair of hands: code reviews, architecture debates, and the freedom to arrive with your own proposals rather than waiting for a ticket.

Your first 3 months are dedicated to ramping up on the Fabriq stack and product, contributing to the AI features already in the hands of beta customers, and shipping your first POCs.

  • Skills and experience

Must-haves:

  • Software engineering depth: 4 to 5 years minimum. Real craftsmanship, clean design decisions, and the ability to explain the architecture trade-offs you made and why.
  • Daily hands-on use of AI to build software. Having never used AI to develop is a deal-breaker on this role.
  • Comfort with ambiguity. You move forward, decide and ship when nothing is specified in advance, and you adapt when the roadmap shifts.
  • Builder mindset with evidence. Concrete examples of things you built from zero, prototyped, tested and iterated on.

Nice-to-haves (optional):

  • A first hands-on experience with agentic systems. Expertise is welcome when it is real: a strong engineer with curiosity and early agentic work beats a self-declared two-year agentic expert who cannot explain concretely what they built.

  • Collaborative posture. The team will evangelise AI across the other product teams. Showing and explaining your work is expected.

Stack:

Build analytics people can trust. Help define what analytics looks like in an AI-first world.

Most analytics platforms ask organisations to trade control for insight.

For almost 20 years, Matomo has shown there is another way: powerful, transparent and trustworthy analytics that respects privacy, gives organisations ownership of their data, and helps people understand what's happening, make better decisions, and improve their work.

More than one million websites use Matomo. That means you'll work on software that is widely used, technically demanding, and close enough to customers that your work has a visible impact. It's a rare opportunity for engineers: solving meaningful, complex product problems while seeing the difference your work makes for customers.

We are independent, profitable, and open source. We are not trying to become a smaller copy of Big Tech analytics platforms. We are building a different kind of analytics company: one where privacy, transparency, customer control, and product quality are part of the core product, not marketing claims.

This role focuses on Matomo Core, the foundation of our product and the platform our open-source users, cloud customers, and wider plugin ecosystem depend on.

If you want unusually high ownership, visible impact, hard product & platform problems, and the opportunity to strengthen a widely used open-source platform, Matomo is worth a serious look.


Why this role matters

Matomo Core is the foundation of our open-source product, cloud platform, plugins, integrations and customer-facing features. 

It has evolved over many years and operates across a wide range of environments, use cases and data volumes. Every improvement to Core benefits customers, open-source users, plugin developers and engineering teams across the Matomo ecosystem. 

We are bringing responsibility for Core into a newly formed European team. You'll help shape how this team works, where it focuses and how it creates the greatest impact across Matomo. 

As a Product Engineer, you’ll help decide where Core can create the greatest impact. That could mean solving a difficult customer problem, strengthening an existing capability, creating a new platform capability, or simplifying the Core platform to make it easier to evolve. 

You’ll work on a mature and technically complex product. The challenge is not simply to preserve what exists. It is to understand why it exists, recognise where it is holding customers or engineers back, and evolve it without disrupting the open-source users, customers, integrations and plugins that already depend on it. 


What you’ll own

You'll own problems, not just code. 

This is not a traditional feature-ticket engineering role. You'll understand customer problems, shape solutions, build across the stack, ship incrementally and continuously improve what you release. AI should be part of your everyday workflow. 

You'll own work from problem to outcome: 

  • Understand the problem before committing to a solution.  

  • Help shape priorities, not just implement them.  

  • Build across the stack wherever the problem takes you.  

  • Ship incrementally and learn from real usage.  

  • Measure outcomes and iterate.  

  • Use AI throughout your workflow. 

    • For senior: You'll help shape what we build, not only how we build it. You'll identify opportunities others haven't seen, influence technical and product direction, and help establish how the Core team operates as it grows. 

    For intermediate: You'll contribute to deciding what we build, working closely with product, engineering and customers rather than simply implementing predefined requirements. You'll own meaningful problems end-to-end while building confidence in navigating ambiguity and product trade-offs. 

    What the work looks like 

    You'll work across the Core platform wherever you can create the greatest impact. 

    Examples include: 

    • Diagnosing and solving complex problems across a large, mature codebase.  

    • Strengthening the security, performance, scalability, reliability and resilience of Matomo.  

    • Protecting the integrity, accuracy and trustworthiness of the data customers rely on.  

    • Strengthen capabilities that support increasingly demanding enterprise use cases.  

    • Building and evolving APIs and platform capabilities used by Matomo plugins and integrations.  

    • Evolving how Matomo handles consent, privacy and responsible data collection. 

    • Advancing server-side tracking, data anonymisation and data-health monitoring. 

    • Enhancing analytics capabilities such as goals, ecommerce reporting and dashboards.

    • Simplifying complex analytics workflows and making powerful functionality easier to use.  

    • Evolving Matomo's design system to create a more consistent and usable product experience. 


How we work

We’re a small team competing with companies many times our size.

That means we optimise for impact.

We value:

  • Customer problems over technical elegance.

  • Shipping over endless planning.

  • Simple solutions over unnecessary complexity.

  • Ownership over handoffs.

  • Iteration over perfection.

  • Clear writing over excessive meetings.

  • Pragmatic engineering over abstract architecture.

  • AI where it helps us move faster.

  • Measuring outcomes over assuming we were right.

    • We care about high standards, but we do not confuse high standards with slow processes. We would rather ship a small useful improvement, learn from it, and improve it than spend months perfecting something before customers see it.

    At the same time, changes to Matomo Core can affect a large number of customers, integrations and plugins. You should be able to move pragmatically while recognising when additional investigation, testing or migration planning is necessary.


What we’re looking for

For senior: You're already operating with a high degree of autonomy. You naturally identify valuable opportunities, make pragmatic decisions in ambiguous situations, and multiply the team's impact through the systems you build, the decisions you influence and the way you approach problems. 

For intermediate: You're already comfortable delivering software independently and are looking to take greater ownership of customer problems, product decisions and technical direction.

Deine Aufgaben

Wir bauen die Software, mit der Mieterstromprojekte laufen: Zählerdaten rein, Abrechnung raus, und alles dazwischen. Das Core Team verantwortet das Betreiberportal, das Produkt, auf dem der laufende Betrieb unserer Kunden steht. Es ist unser fachlich tiefstes Team, und es wächst.

Das Betreiberportal ist kein generisches SaaS. Es bildet die Energiewirtschaft ab: Messstellenbetrieb, Marktkommunikation, Netzentgelte, Umlagen, Abrechnung nach Regeln, die der Gesetzgeber schreibt und regelmäßig ändert. Wer hier priorisiert, muss verstehen, was eine Anforderung für den Betreiber wirtschaftlich bedeutet und was passiert, wenn sie falsch umgesetzt wird.

Dafür suchen wir eine Person, die das Team führt und das Geschäft dahinter versteht. Nicht als Durchreiche für Tickets und nicht als Architekt, der alles selbst entscheidet, sondern als jemand, der Business-Anforderungen in technische Entscheidungen übersetzt und dafür sorgt, dass gute Entwickler gute Arbeit machen können: klare Ziele, wenig Reibung, ehrliches Feedback, verlässliche Lieferung.

Der Weg dahin ist bewusst gewählt: Du startest für rund sechs Monate als Entwickler im Core Team. Du baust Features, machst Reviews und lernst Codebasis, Fachlichkeit und Menschen von innen kennen. Danach übernimmst du die Führung des Teams. Wer ein Team führen will, das er nie von innen gesehen hat, führt es an dem vorbei, was zählt.

Technisch: Python mit Django und Django Ninja im Backend, React mit TypeScript im Frontend, PostgreSQL mit TimescaleDB, deployt auf Kubernetes per GitOps mit ArgoCD. KI-Coding-Assistenten sind fester Teil des Workflows. In den ersten Monaten schreibst du diesen Code selbst. Danach musst du ihn weiter lesen können und verstehen, worüber dein Team diskutiert.

In den ersten sechs Monaten

  • Du arbeitest als Entwickler im Core Team: Features end-to-end, Reviews, Deployments, Support-Fälle. Ohne Sonderrolle

  • Du lernst die Fachlichkeit von Messkonzept bis Abrechnung und die Geschichte der Codebasis, inklusive der Stellen, an denen sie weh tut

  • Du baust Vertrauen zu den Menschen im Team auf, weil du mit ihnen arbeitest und nicht über ihnen

Danach

  • Du führst das Core Team: Einstellung, Onboarding, 1:1s, Entwicklung, Feedback. Die Menschen im Team sind deine erste Verantwortung

  • Du verantwortest die Lieferung: Zusammen mit Product priorisierst du nach wirtschaftlichem Wert und regulatorischem Druck, planst realistisch und sorgst dafür, dass Zugesagtes fertig wird

  • Du bringst Fachverständnis in die Produktentscheidungen ein: Du erkennst, wann eine Anforderung aus dem Markt kommt, wann aus einem einzelnen Kunden, und wann aus einem Missverständnis

  • Du hältst die technische Qualität hoch, ohne selbst der Flaschenhals zu sein: Du moderierst Architekturentscheidungen, forderst Tests und Reviews ein und schaffst Raum für Refactoring

  • Du bist die Schnittstelle zu Product, Support und den anderen Engineering-Teams, und du löst Konflikte, bevor sie im Sprint landen

  • Du machst Probleme sichtbar: Wenn etwas nicht klappt, sagst du es früh und mit Vorschlag statt spät und mit Ausrede

  • Du gestaltest Prozesse so, dass sie dem Team dienen, und schaffst die ab, die es nicht tun


Dein Profil

  • Mehrere Jahre Erfahrung als Softwareentwickler mit Web-Anwendungen in Produktion. Du kannst in Django und React produktiv arbeiten oder dich in wenigen Wochen dort einfinden

  • Erfahrung in der Führung eines Entwicklungsteams, als Engineering Manager, Team Lead oder in einer vergleichbaren Rolle mit Personalverantwortung

  • Du kannst ein Datenmodell beurteilen und eine Architekturdiskussion moderieren, ohne sie an dich zu reißen

  • Du willst wieder oder weiter Code schreiben, bevor du führst, und siehst das als Vorteil, nicht als Umweg

  • Erfahrung in der Energiewirtschaft, idealerweise in Messstellenbetrieb, Abrechnung, Marktkommunikation oder Mieterstrom. Du kennst Begriffe wie Messkonzept, MaLo oder OBIS nicht nur aus Wikipedia

  • Business-Verständnis: Du denkst vom Geschäftsmodell des Betreibers her, nicht vom Feature. Du kannst erklären, welche Anforderung Umsatz sichert, welche Risiko reduziert und welche nur schön ist

  • Du gibst direktes Feedback und hältst es aus, direktes Feedback zu bekommen

  • Du kannst Nein sagen, zu Stakeholdern und zum eigenen Team, und begründen, warum

  • Du fühlst dich in einem Startup wohl, in dem Strukturen noch entstehen und du sie mitgestaltest

  • Deutsch mindestens auf C1-Niveau, weil Fachlichkeit, Kunden und ein Großteil der Kommunikation deutsch sind


Warum wir?

  • Eine Führungsrolle mit echtem Gestaltungsspielraum in einer wachsenden Engineering-Organisation, mit einem Einstieg, der dich nicht ins kalte Wasser wirft

  • Direkter Draht zum CTO und Mitsprache bei der Teamstruktur, nicht nur bei der Umsetzung

  • Hybrid in Hamburg: 1-2 Tage im Office, der Rest remote
